name: Whataboutism pivot
what_it_looks_like: A question about a rival state is answered with a US crime, and the original question is never answered.
example: "What about Iraq?" in reply to Xinjiang; "and you are lynching Negroes"
caution: A US comparison is fine when the speaker also answers the question. Count it only when the pivot replaces the answer.

name: One-directional skepticism
what_it_looks_like: Claims against the US are accepted on thin evidence; claims against Russia, China or Iran need impossible proof ("where are the bodies", "source: Radio Free Asia").
example: Dismissing a report by its funder alone; demanding satellite photos, then calling them fake
source: Balci et al. (source-sharing: 60% of tankie news links go to Chinese and Russian state outlets)
caution: Skepticism of one report is normal. The marker is the asymmetry across topics.

name: Agency denial
what_it_looks_like: Only the US acts. Everyone else reacts: Russia was provoked, protesters are paid, Hamas was created by conditions.
example: "Russia had no choice"; "what did you expect them to do"
caution: Explaining a cause is not denying agency. Look for the missing sentence that assigns the other side any responsibility.

name: The pro-America test
what_it_looks_like: The speaker cannot say anything positive about the US, or condemn a rival state, without an immediate "but".
example: "Critical of both, but the US is worse"; no flag, no "we"
source: Smith at 00:35-00:39 ("that's the litmus test"); Destiny at NEF0VNPZ7lU 00:15
caution: Smith's test, not a validated measure. Many people dislike patriotism without being campist; use it on public figures' stated positions, not on anonymous commenters.

name: Selective anti-imperialism
what_it_looks_like: "Imperialism" is used only for the US and its allies; Russian, Chinese or Iranian actions abroad never get the word.
example: "Russia isn't imperialist, it doesn't export finance capital"
caution: This is the cleanest split between campists and the anti-campist left, who call both imperialist.

name: Ukraine cross-check
what_it_looks_like: An account posting a sweeping anti-American claim usually has a pro-Russia or anti-Ukraine record.
caution: Destiny's heuristic for public commentators. For Reddit accounts this is the position-bundle analysis the project already does on hashed IDs; do not publish it per account.

name: Two faces
what_it_looks_like: Moderate framing in liberal venues ("we just want healthcare"), open revolutionary or anti-party framing on home channels.
example: Compare a guest spot on mainstream TV with the same person's own stream
caution: A claim about named public figures; needs both clips with timestamps before it is repeated.

name: Ride-or-die factionalism
what_it_looks_like: Every candidate on the team is defended whatever they said; every Democrat outside it is an enemy; fights start right after Democratic wins.
example: Leadership challenges the week after the midterms
caution: Testable on the Reddit data as timing: does anti-Democrat volume rise after Democratic wins? Needs a prediction file first.

name: Relabeling
what_it_looks_like: Standard Democratic policy is claimed as socialist when it is popular, while the party is called right-wing.
example: "We need a left that fights for higher taxes on the rich" as an argument against Democrats
caution: Destiny's observation; the same facts read differently from the left (moving the party).

name: Borrowed protection
what_it_looks_like: Criticism of a movement figure is answered as bigotry against the figure's group.
caution: Smith's claim and a contested one: real anti-Muslim bigotry is common, so each case needs reading. Do not code automatically.
